summary: Jackson County, OR tower at Railroad Gap: 15-foot L-4 built 1933, Air Warning post 1942-43, removed 1951; a 2018 report describes only a later shelter cabin's foundation.

facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1951 (register, Forest Lookouts) or destroyed that year (firelookout.com). A 2018 report describes only the concrete foundation of a later shelter cabin.

access.note: A 2018 hiking report describes reaching the Gap on the Cow Creek Trail (USFS #1424) from Forest Road 3232. No source says whether the trail is open now.

visit.trail_note: 2018 report: summer round trip to the Gap is about 12 miles on the Cow Creek Trail. The tower is gone; the foundation described is the shelter cabin's, not the lookout's.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Forest Lookouts page date the tower to 1933, but a July 1932 paper says a lookout is to be built on the Gap and a late-July 1932 item places a husband at the Railroad Gap lookout. The story reports both.
The register says the tower was used all year as an AWS post in 1942. Forest Lookouts gives an activation date of August 24, 1942. The story gives both and says they disagree.
The register, Forest Lookouts and the 2018 report say removed in 1951; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1951. The story says removed and notes the other source's wording.

sources.title: Hiking Through Old-Growth Along Southwest Oregon's Cow Creek

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: L-4 design and 4.6 m height (15 ft) agree with the sources. Today's status rests on a 2018 hiking blog; the concrete foundation belongs to a later shelter cabin, not the lookout. Access is inferred from that blog's trail description, so the access note is dated 2018. Staffing as_of 1941 is the fire-season reference; the 1942 Redifer item is in the story.
